text:
ashley: heads-up — drafting a short playbook for Dedicated provisioning across regions. need a quick sanity check on GPU mix + concurrency targets. TL;DR: want to avoid overprovisioning for bursty chat workloads while keeping p99 latency under 450ms for 8k context.

ben: love it. are we assuming quantized models (q8/q4) for the p99 target or FP16? that'll change throughput a lot.

ashley: primary plan is q4f16 for h100 in us-west and q8 for a100 in eu-west as fallback. target concurrency per-GPU: 16 for h100 q4f16, 8 for a100 q8. open to numbers.

cheng: that concurrency looks optimistic for chat with long prefix caching churn. do you have batching assumptions? e.g., dynamic batching up to 128 tokens and 40 reqs/batch?

ashley: good call. playbook assumes workload-aware batching: dynamic batch window 10ms, max batch size 48 requests or 1024 tokens, whichever first. we tune per-pool.

dana: can we add a conservative autoscale headroom rule? suggestion: reserved buffer of +30% capacity vs forecasted 95th percentile QPS, and immediate burst queue that can scale to +50% with prewarmed instances.

ben: +1 on headroom. also recommend re-routing policy for region mismatch: prefer local pool until 90th percentile, then failover to neighboring region rather than lower-tier model. reduces cross-region latency spikes.

ashley: noted. the playbook draft has three tiers: steady (baseline commit), burst (prewarmed burst nodes), emergency (cross-region fallback). will document failover thresholds.

cheng: kernel choices: are we standardizing on fused attention kernels on h100 and fallback to optimized matmul kernels on a100? that affects latency variance and kernel load balancing.

ashley: yes — h100: fused-attention + Triton custom ops for q4f16. a100: optimized cuBLAS/cuDNN matmul path with custom KV-cache tweaks. include a /kernels table in the doc.

dana: for quant experiments, include a short A/B eval plan: 5% traffic for q4f16 vs fp16 baseline, eval prompt-set (1000 prompts), check ROUGE + hallucination rate + latency tail. flag any >2% quality delta.

ben: add cost-per-token projection per pool in the playbook. show throughput vs cost curves for h100-a100-qmix so product can pick capacity vs budget.

ashley: will add charts. quick question: concurrency target per GPU should be expressed as "soft" concurrency (queued requests accepted) vs hard concurrency (active tokens). which do we want?

cheng: soft concurrency is easier operationally; hard concurrency maps to throughput better. propose both: soft_target=20, hard_active_target=16 for h100 q4f16. soft_target=10, hard_active_target=8 for a100 q8.

dana: also include a warmup checklist for burst nodes: load model weights to GPU, run two synthetic warmup queries (long prefix + short reply) to populate KV caches, then rotate into LB. otherwise first few requests blow up p99.

ashley: perfect—I'll add that. infra-bot: posting current pool util numbers for reference.

infra-bot: current pools snapshot: us-west-h100-pool: 72% avg util, p95 latency 310ms, concurrency avg 13. eu-west-a100-pool: 59% avg util, p95 latency 420ms, concurrency avg 6.

ben: those snapshots validate our targets. us-west can safely add burst nodes with +30% headroom; eu-west should prioritize kernel optimizations to get p95 down.

cheng: one more nit: add a policy for quantization regression detection. daily evals on canonical prompt-suite and an automatic rollback trigger if quality drops >1.5% or hallucination delta >1%.

dana: include a short runbook snippet for scaling events: steps to verify model health, check KV cache miss rates, check kernel saturation, and how to manually toggle routing to fallback. Keep it <=6 bullets.

ashley: will ship draft by EOD. anyone want to add specific chart breaks? I'm planning: latency vs concurrency curves per GPU, throughput vs cost per token, and a kernel saturation heatmap.

ben: add region comparison chart (us-west vs eu-west) for identical config to show perf delta. product loves that.

cheng: also include a small table of common knob values: batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, soft_target, hard_active_target, burst_headroom_pct.

dana: thanks — this looks very actionable. if you want, I can pair on the rollback thresholds and runbook bullets for the burst play.

ashley: appreciate it. I'll ping for a quick review after first pass. :thumbsup:

ben: thanks ashley — excited to have a concise playbook for Dedicated provisioning.

ashley: end of thread — attaching the draft doc link when done: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-playbook (will replace with final link)
